chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Taymi, from Ja'far ibn Bakr, from Abdullah ibn Abi Sahl, from Abdullah ibn Abdul Kareem, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three [things] are from the good fortune: the obedient wife, and the righteous children, and the man who is granted his livelihood in his own city, going out to his family in the morning and returning in the evening.'

key_terms.الزَّوْجَةُ الْمُؤَاتِيَة: The obedient wife (one who fulfills duties and is agreeable)
key_terms.الْأَوْلَادُ الْبَارُّون: The righteous children (those who are dutiful to parents)

ai.seo_question: What are the three things that constitute good fortune according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines three pillars of worldly and spiritual felicity, emphasizing the stability of the family unit through a dutiful spouse and righteous offspring. He further highlights the virtue of local livelihood, which preserves family cohesion by allowing the husband to remain present with his household, a concept deeply valued in Shia social ethics for maintaining domestic tranquility and religious observance.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Husayn Al Taymi, from Ja’far Bin Bakr, from Abdullah Bin Abu Sahl, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Kareem who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Three are from the good fortune – the obedient wife, and the righteous children, and the man who achieves the sustenance of his livelihood in his own city, and is present with his family (every morning and in the evenings)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn Al-Husayn al-Tamimiy from Ja’far ibn Bakr from ‘Abd Allah ibn abu Sahl ibn ‘Abd al-Karim who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Three factors help a man enjoy good fortune: One is a cooperating wife, virtuous and kind children, and he finds his living where he lives and is present in his family every morning and evenings.’”
